title: She Returned A Vacuum. The Serial Number Returned Her.
script: A customer returned a premium vacuum and said it had never worked. The box looked new. The vacuum inside looked like it had cleaned a gravel driveway. She demanded a cash refund and handed me a receipt from the previous afternoon. Our policy allowed it, but the serial number on the receipt did not match the machine. She said manufacturers reuse numbers. They do not. I checked the rewards account attached to her receipt. It showed yesterday’s new vacuum—and another purchase of the same model eighteen months earlier. The old purchase matched the battered machine in front of me. She had put her old vacuum in the new box and brought it back. Inventory magic, minus the magic. I denied the refund and returned both items to her. She threatened a chargeback, so I printed both serial records and noted the attempted switch on her account. The chargeback never arrived. The gravel did, scattered across my counter.
